decision: Do not migrate the existing Codex/Claude production routes to stock acpx 0.20.0. Claude loses the original overload identity even with AIR negotiation. Codex capacity can be repaired by a custom negotiation proxy plus terminal metadata interpretation, but that is a separate, vendor-extension-dependent integration; it is not the tested 99-line stock bridge and does not justify deleting mixed policy/transport files wholesale. No production wrapper is removed.
scope: Real Codex and Claude native executables, real ACP adapters and published acpx runtime. Only model HTTP responses are deterministic local fixtures; no real vendor inference or billing. User configuration and live workers are not changed.

findings: Trusted native SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse and Stop hooks run through both adapters. PreToolUse denial prevents the attempted write. The Codex app-server ignores the CLI bypass-hook-trust switch; explicit fixture trust hashes resolve this configuration difference. It is not lack of native-hook support.

Both latest adapters pass a real positive write control, a native-hook deny control, a workspace-outside write denial and a read-only write denial. Test directories and TMPDIR were shortened to avoid a native Claude Unix socket path initialization failure; no sandbox initialization error was accepted as proof of confinement.

The Codex adapter turns the injected terminal HTTP 503 capacity failure into assistant text and a successful end_turn. The receipt bridge therefore returns exit 0/returned; the same marker words in ordinary assistant output must not trigger capacity. Existing agx returns capacity/75 on the native structured error. The defect also reproduces in the latest compatible 1.x adapter and latest 2.2.2.

Claude's native HTTP 529 produces typed api_retry error_status=529/error=overloaded. The adapter's retry information is negotiated through an AIR sessionFailure extension, which the tested public acpx runtime does not expose to this consumer. The bridge retries five times and ends as timeout rather than capacity/75. The latest adapter 0.94.0 reproduces the failure under supported Node 24 as well.

A real baseline bug was found: agx only recognized overloaded_error/API Error: 529 strings, missing the native 2.1.306 api_retry error_status field. A failing regression was added first; capacity.ts now recognizes exactly the typed system/api_retry/529 shape. The native baseline then stops with exit 75 after one API attempt; rate-limit 429 and quoted assistant text remain noncapacity.

With codex-acp 1.13.1 (the latest version within acpx's declared ^1.1.5 range), the tested read-only mode allowed the inside-marker write. Native agx denied it, and codex-acp 2.2.2 denied it. This is a preserved local compatibility counterexample, not a claim about all deployments of 1.13.1. The final rejection does not rely on this older adapter mismatch: the latest adapters still fail capacity.

A wire-proxy recheck advertised AIR sessionFailure without modifying the released adapters. Codex then retained the 503 error in wire metadata, but the stock runtime bridge still returned success. Claude HTTP 529 overload and HTTP 500 api_error emitted identical first failure category/severity/title/actions (service/warning/Retrying Claude, attempt 1 of 10./[]), omitting original HTTP status and error kind. Both retried five model calls before timeout. Extension negotiation alone does not restore typed overload identity.

upper_bound_transport_and_parsers.caveat: Whole-file upper bounds include CLI policy, receipts and lifecycle logic; not a claim that all lines become safely removable.

required_retained_concerns: worker environment and host isolation declaration
capacity provenance, model cooldown and continuation rules
run ledger, ticket provenance, verification, acceptance and jj workspace lifecycle
required_upstream_changes_for_a_viable_r: Expose supported capability negotiation in the client (rather than requiring an independently maintained protocol proxy). Codex terminal failure metadata is already preserved in public result._meta and needs correct consumption, not invented text provenance.
Preserve Claude native error_status and error kind before the SDK retries. Tested AIR warning fields alone cannot distinguish HTTP 529 overload from HTTP 500 api_error.
code_comparison.reason: The 99-line bridge is executable and satisfies normal execution/hooks/latest sandbox cases, but fails two mandatory capacity contracts. Deleting native wrappers would remove working capacity behavior or require preserving them beside acpx, which does not constitute the proposed replacement.

corrections_during_testing: An initial bridge assertion expected an iterator to reject; acpx startTurn reports terminal failures through turn.result. The bridge now consumes the documented result.

An initial Codex positive test expected top-level tools, but native 0.163 exposes code-mode tools through additional_tools. The model fixture now emits the correct custom tool call and text deltas; actual filesystem writes prove the control.
Early long fixture paths caused Claude sandbox bridge socket initialization failure. Final accepted positive/negative sandbox controls use short, run-owned TMPDIR paths.
The first adapter versions were range minima. Latest compatible and latest released adapters were subsequently tested; final adoption rejection uses current released versions, not only old minima.

Rechecking the AIR proxy exposed public terminal result._meta for Codex. Interpreting its typed failure restored capacity/75 and preserved the quoted-text control. Therefore the earlier stock-bridge failure must not be described as fundamental Codex/ACP incompatibility or loss of all terminal metadata. With provider HTTP retries=3, both the native control and repaired bridge made four API calls; the one-call claim applies only to the zero-provider-retry controls.
